ILLUSTRATIVE

Intent Centre: run a session from start to signed charter

A step-by-step guide with screens, for the first Signal Harbor module. Everything shown is practice data for an illustrative family office. No real client is shown.

Who does what

OrganiserPrepares the session, shares the link, runs the briefing, closes the private rooms, fixes the groups, brings the room back together and starts the charter.
ParticipantJoins with the link (no account needed), works in a private room with North, submits notes, then votes and comments when everyone is back together.
ApproverA named person who signs the charter. Nothing is signed until a person signs it.

Your privacy, in plain words

  • Private rooms are private. What you write in your private room is visible only to you and North until you choose to submit it. The organiser sees how many notes are in, never what they say.
  • Anonymous is your choice, note by note. An anonymous note shows no name to anyone, including the organiser and administrators.
  • Your information stays on your company's own system. The only thing that ever leaves is masked text: names and company words are swapped for neutral tokens first.
  • Suggestions are only suggestions. North and Nira offer help, clearly marked. Your company decides.

The helpers are named by what they do: North is the industry expert, Nira is the guide.

Get ready

1

Open the Intent tile Organiser

Sign in and open the Intent tile on your home page. This is where every session starts.

2

Start a new session Organiser

The Intent Centre lists your sessions. Choose Prepare a session.

3

Say what the session is for Organiser

Write in one or two sentences what the session is for, and the outcome you want. Everyone reads this at the briefing.

4

Choose people and time Organiser

Pick how many people will join (one to ten) and how long the session lasts. The time is shared between the briefing, the private rooms and the time together. The three parts must add up to the total.

5

Decide what North may offer Organiser

North is the industry expert. You can let North offer common industry practice and a library of common problems. Everything North offers is a suggestion. Your company decides.

6

Choose the briefing video Organiser

Choose the standard briefing video, or no video. The written rules are always shown as well.

7

Check and save a draft Organiser

Read your choices on one page, then press Save draft. You can change a draft until the session starts.

Invite people

8

Start the room and share the link Organiser

Press Start the room. You get a join link. Share it only with the people you invite. Making a new link stops the old one working.

9

Take your own seat Organiser

If you will take part yourself, choose Join as a participant, pick a seat and give your role.

10

Guests join with the link Participant

A guest opens the link, picks a free seat and types a name and a role. No account is needed.

11

Wait in the lobby Participant

In the lobby, Nira, the guide, welcomes you. You can see who has arrived while you wait for the organiser.

The briefing

12

Start the briefing Organiser

When people have arrived, press Start the briefing, then Open the briefing. You can start with empty seats; late arrivals see the briefing first.

13

Read the room rules Everyone

The briefing shows the video (or a placeholder) and the room rules in writing: what the session is for, what we want to leave with, how the time is shared and how notes are shown.

14

Add minutes if you need them Organiser

Running short? Press Add 2, 5 or 10 minutes. The clock goes up at once.

15

Say I'm clear Everyone

Press I'm clear when the rules are understood, or ask Nira what is not clear. The page shows how many people say they are clear.

16

Send everyone to their rooms Organiser

Press Send everyone to their rooms. You do not have to wait for everyone to be clear. The private-room clock starts.

Private rooms

17

Your private room Participant

Only you and North can see your room. Nobody else sees what you write here, including the organiser.

18

Talk it through with North Participant

Write in your own words and press Enter. North asks questions and offers common industry practice, always marked as a suggestion.

19

Save what matters as notes Participant

Press Save as a note to keep a thought. North reads it back in your words. Notes stay drafts, private to you, until you submit them.

20

Add the details Participant

Under each note you can add why it matters, who is affected, how often and how big. Only you give the number you believe. North never suggests one.

21

Choose by name or anonymous Participant

For each note, choose By name or Anonymous. If anonymous, nobody can see who wrote it: not the organiser and not an administrator.

22

Submit and say I'm done Participant

Submit each note you are happy with. A submitted note cannot be changed. Then press I'm done to leave your room.

Together on the board

23

Wait for the notes Organiser

While rooms are open, you see only how many notes are in, not what they say.

24

End the private session early Organiser

If everyone is done, or time is short, press Close the rooms now, then confirm. Notes already submitted are kept.

25

See the brainstorm board Everyone

The notes appear together. North groups similar notes and says why. The grouping is a suggestion. Anonymous notes show no name.

26

Fix the groups and bring everyone back Organiser

The organiser can rename, split or move notes. When the groups look right, press Bring everyone back in the room.

Back in the room

27

Vote, agree and comment Everyone

For each group, everyone votes Must, Should, Could or Not this time. You can agree and add a short comment. Tick the groups that go into the charter.

28

Finish early with the done button Organiser

When the room has talked enough, press We're done, go to the charter. If every group is already decided, Nira offers the same step.

The charter

29

Check the charter Organiser

North drafts a short line for each agreed problem, beginning So that. Use it as it is or edit it. Notes the room left out are listed as left for later.

30

Sign Approver

A named person signs. This version needs two signatures. If the seniors are in the room they sign there and then. Otherwise name an approver when you prepare the session.

31

Signed and read-only Approver

Once both have signed, the charter is read-only. It can be downloaded, and it goes on to the next module. A change needs a new sign-off.

If you get stuck

The time is running outPress Add 2 minutes, Add 5 minutes or Add 10 minutes at the top of the briefing, the private rooms, the board or the room. The clock goes up at once. Only the organiser can add time.
End the private session earlyThe organiser opens the board and presses Close the rooms now, then confirms. Notes already submitted are kept; drafts that were not submitted are posted to the board for their writers, anonymously when each person chooses how a note shows, and under the writer's name only when the organiser set every note to show names.
The room has talked enoughThe organiser presses We're done, go to the charter (or Finish and go to the charter when Nira says every problem is decided). If some groups are still open you are asked once to confirm.
A person cannot joinMake a new link on the organiser page. The old link stops working; people already seated stay seated. A seat that has been removed cannot be used again.
North or Nira does not answerYour notes are still saved. You can carry on writing; North's help is a bonus, not a requirement.

Illustrative guide. Screens taken from a practice session with made-up data.
